cōnsōbrīnus, cōnsōbrīnī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

cousin (male)

Other words

  • cōnsōbrīna, cōnsōbrīnae f. — cousin (female)

    noun, first declension · classical · Traupman 24; Traupman 298 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • patruēlis, patruēlis m./f. — a cousin on the father’s side: a father’s brother’s child

    noun, third declension; also an adjective, frāter patruēlis · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.1: L. Cicerō frāter noster cognātiōne patruēlis, amōre germānus (Lewis & Short); Suet. Dom. 15 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 24; Traupman 298 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Latin names a cousin by the parents: patruēlis is the child of two brothers, cōnsōbrīnus, cōnsōbrīna strictly the child of two sisters (Lewis & Short, after the Digest), though it is also used loosely of any first cousin. Traupman glosses cōnsōbrīnus “sister’s son” and patruēlis “brother’s child”, meaning the parent’s sister and brother.
